claim: Self-attention's time and memory complexity is quadratic in sequence length, which is why a 32k-context training step is memory-bound before any sparse-attention trick is applied.
stance_target: The repo's claim that CSA2 at 32k is worth testing because full attention's activation memory is the binding term
scope_conditions: Standard Transformer self-attention; sequence lengths up to 64K
quoted_support: Transformers are slow and memory-hungry on long sequences, since the time and memory complexity of self-attention are quadratic in sequence length.
numbers: quadratic time and memory in sequence length

claim: The missing principle in prior attention work is IO-awareness: tiling the QK^T, softmax and V computation so the N x N score matrix is never written to HBM reduces memory reads and writes, and the resulting algorithm is IO-optimal over a range of SRAM sizes.
stance_target: Whether a 32k-context run can avoid materializing full attention matrices on a 64 GB card
scope_conditions: GPU memory hierarchy (HBM versus on-chip SRAM); tiling with online softmax
quoted_support: We propose FlashAttention, an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce the number of memory reads/writes between GPU high bandwidth memory (HBM) and GPU on-chip SRAM.

claim: FlashAttention and block-sparse FlashAttention have the same memory footprint, which grows linearly rather than quadratically with sequence length, so the quadratic activation term is removed for both dense and sparse attention.
stance_target: The comparison design for CSA2 versus full attention at 32k: both arms must use FlashAttention or the memory comparison is meaningless
scope_conditions: Forward and backward passes; measured memory footprint versus sequence length
quoted_support: and block-sparse FlashAttention have the same memory footprint, which grows linearly with sequence length

claim: FlashAttention delivers 15% end-to-end wall-clock speedup on BERT-large at sequence length 512, 3x on GPT-2 at 1K and 2.4x on long-range arena at 1K-4K, so the speedup grows with sequence length.
stance_target: The expected throughput benefit of an IO-aware attention kernel at 32k context on this box
scope_conditions: A100-class GPUs; BERT-large, GPT-2, long-range arena; sequence lengths 512 to 4K
quoted_support: FlashAttention trains Transformers faster than existing baselines: 15% end-to-end wall-clock speedup on BERT-large (seq. length 512) compared to the MLPerf 1.1 training speed record, 3× speedup on GPT-2 (seq. length 1K), and 2.4× speedup on long-range arena (seq. length 1K-4K).

claim: Block-sparse FlashAttention is faster than any existing approximate attention method, which makes it the natural baseline against which a CSA2-style sparse attention kernel should be compared at 32k.
stance_target: Whether CSA2's claimed win survives comparison against a block-sparse FlashAttention baseline rather than dense attention
quoted_support: We also extend FlashAttention to block-sparse attention, yielding an approximate attention algorithm that is faster than any existing approximate attention method.

claim: Long-context capability comes from the kernel, not only from sparsity: FlashAttention enables better-than-chance results at 16K and 64K sequence lengths where standard attention could not fit.
stance_target: Whether 32k training on 64 GB cards needs CSA2 at all, or whether a dense FlashAttention kernel suffices
scope_conditions: Path-X (16K) and Path-256 (64K) benchmarks; GPT-2 quality at longer context
quoted_support: FlashAttention and block-sparse FlashAttention enable longer context in Transformers, yielding higher quality models (0.7 better perplexity on GPT-2 and 6.4 points of lift on long-document classification) and entirely new capabilities: the first Transformers to achieve better-than-chance performance on the Path-X challenge (seq. length 16K, 61.4% accuracy) and Path-256 (seq. length 64K, 63.1% accuracy).
